title: Crawler revamp, Phase 2: the crawler as one service, and its console
why: decisions/0160 §2: one 5-minute run did every workflow's work in a fixed order and starved the later ones, and every run showed 'succeeded' on Railway. Now the site plans each run: each workflow (W1 listings, W2 upkeep, W3 sources, W6 heritage, W9 landmarks, W11 how-to guides, W12 search learning) has its share; finding businesses goes first, then whoever waited longest; a task not reached is never a failure and goes first next time; the bulk loads run only at night after the run's own work. Each run reports task by task (crawl_runs, crawl_run_items); a run that can't work is a failed run on Railway, and Pulse opens a case when no run has started for 30 minutes or six runs fail (replacing the false 'crawler has stopped' alert). One queue of requests (crawl_requests) for the workflows that move onto it next. The cost ledger (crawl_costs) counts the worker's paid calls, failed ones included; Claude's paid answers that then fail are now counted (D16), and Tavily page reads count fully and against the search plan (D17). Insights -> Crawler is the console (Jason chose Insights): each workflow's tasks, queue, last runs, spend; Pause, Resume, share, Run first, Switch off, Retry failed, greyed out with the reason for those who can't. The worker change (contract 2) deploys from main after this is live; until then the worker runs as before. The database update only adds tables.
